title: A string library built from its reference
hints: Write each function's examples from its page as tests in your head before coding: the empty input, the input with nothing to do, and every special rule ("an empty `s` gives one empty string", "an empty `from` matches between characters").
`split` and `splitWhitespace` disagree on purpose about empty input and repeated separators. If one of your results is surprising, re-read that function's own page rather than the other's.
requirements: Every function matches its page, including empty inputs and the `maxSplit` and `maxCount` limits.
`split` refuses an empty separator with the documented exception.
`splitLines` treats `\r\n` as a single boundary and never adds a trailing empty line.
stretch: Add `partition(s, sep)`, documented as returning three strings: the part before the first `sep`, `sep` itself, and the part after; if `sep` is not found, `s` and two empty strings. Write its reference page first, then the code.
